children: A softer-than-expected rise in underlying consumer prices is likely to keep the Federal Reserve from tightening policy next week, even as rising energy and computer memory costs put renewed pressure on goods inflation, according to Pantheon Macroeconomics.
Pantheon expects August core CPI to rise 0.17% month over month, below the thresholds it believes could prompt FOMC members to tighten policy.
A 0.21% monthly increase would leave the year-over-year rate at 2.5%, while a reading of no more than 0.28% would bring the annual rate down to 2.4%, according to the note.
The firm said that the breadth of the CPI increase will also matter, particularly for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, while some policymakers are likely to focus on the implications for the core PCE deflator.
Pantheon expects its 0.17% forecast to undershoot all of these thresholds, leading the FOMC to keep policy unchanged this month.
The report said it expects core goods prices to rise about 0.2% in August as higher energy and computer memory costs work through supply chains.

Prices for processed materials used to produce finished goods have risen sharply since spring, with Pantheon noting that changes in those input prices typically feed into finished consumer goods and core goods inflation with a lag of about six months.

Services inflation, meanwhile, is expected to remain relatively contained. Pantheon said it expects airline fares to fall, while residual seasonal patterns limit increases across several service categories. It also forecasted primary rent to rise 0.22% and owners' equivalent rent to increase 0.25%.
The report also forecasted a 0.3% rise in headline CPI, driven partly by a 4.4% increase in energy goods prices, while core CPI is expected to rise 0.2% in the broader release.

title: August CPI likely keeps Fed on hold, Pantheon says
